Summary: Atomic subprocess for creating or validating a named .NET solution, app project, test project, project references, and first build proof using the application archetype grounded by the parent scope.
ValueStatement: Turns the fragile first implementation step into a small observable child process with explicit naming, scaffold, test-project, and build validation checkpoints without hardcoding a specific app archetype.
InterfaceContractSummary: The parent process supplies the solution name, project names, product root, app archetype, target framework, test framework preference, and any existing constraints; this subprocess returns scaffold and first-build evidence.
GovernanceNotes: Do not hide scaffold failures behind later implementation steps. Naming, project layout, test-project inclusion, and build output must be observable before feature work starts.
ChangeSummary: Introduces a reusable child process for generic .NET bootstrap lanes required by larger software-development processes.
GovernancePolicySummary: A development slice may proceed only after the solution scaffold and test project are present or explicitly documented as already existing.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: The scaffolded solution, app project, and test project are durable process artifacts, not transient agent chat decisions.
OperatingModeSummary: Assisted execution with explicit manager observation is sufficient because each step has a narrow, verifiable output.
SimulationReadinessSummary: Small enough for local validation and nested subprocess tests while still representing a real .NET project bootstrap.
Metrics: Time from naming contract to first successful solution build.
Percentage of scaffold runs with an included test project and project reference.
Number of scaffold defects discovered after implementation work begins.
Risks: Wrong solution or project names leak into generated namespaces and test references.
Test project omitted or disconnected from the application project.
Template command succeeds but first build fails because dependencies or target frameworks are wrong.
TailoringRules: For an existing repository, keep this subprocess only when the solution skeleton is missing or materially wrong.

Select the project template from current-run project structure or upstream architecture notes. Do not let generic examples or remembered prior runs provide the stack. Escalate when the stack or archetype is missing or conflicts with requested validation.
Select the test project template from the parent contract or existing repository convention. Do not hardcode xUnit, MSTest, or NUnit in the process.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Track scaffold readiness, blockers, and handoff evidence for the parent process.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A manager-capable human or AI agent that can summarize progress and escalate missing inputs.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Create the requested .NET solution, app project, test project, and references from the scaffold contract without assuming a UI stack, service shape, or default test framework.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A general .NET-capable implementer with access to repository files and build tools; must choose app and test templates only from current-run project structure or upstream artifacts.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Confirm the solution builds and the test project is usable before handoff.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A reviewer that can evaluate build and test evidence.

Steps.Title: Capture solution scaffold contract
Steps.Subtitle: Names before files
Steps.Notes: Record solution name, app project name, app project directory, test project name, test project directory, target framework, product root, requested .NET archetype, test framework preference, and allowed template switches. Use the grounded product root from project structure or parent artifacts. If no product root is grounded, block unless the parent explicitly defines a managed output root as the product. For greenfield .NET apps, keep the solution file at the product root, the app project under productRoot/src, and the test project under productRoot/tests unless the parent contract says otherwise. Copy explicit project-structure values exactly and do not add unrequested features, framework defaults, or test-framework defaults.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Parent process request with target product root, solution name, project names, app archetype, test framework preference, and framework constraints.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Unambiguous scaffold contract ready for execution, including solution file candidates and app/test project directories.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Recorded names, product root, solution file candidates, project paths, target framework, app archetype, test framework preference, and assumptions.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Setup manager can clarify names but cannot invent externally visible project identity when the parent contract is explicit.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block when naming, product root, app archetype, test framework, or repository target is ambiguous enough to create the wrong files.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can report blockers to the parent run.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Scaffold contract
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Used by child and parent managers to verify generated names and paths.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name the solution, solution file candidates, app project and directory, test project and directory, target framework, product root, app archetype/template, test framework/template, and whether the product root already exists or must be created.

Steps.Title: Create .NET solution and app project
Steps.Subtitle: Solution skeleton
Steps.Notes: Create the solution file and requested .NET app project with the agreed names, paths, archetype, and template. Use workspace_create_directory for the grounded product root and productRoot/src when they do not exist. Use workspace_dotnet_new with template sln for the solution at the product root, inspect the resulting .slnx or .sln file, then scaffold the app under productRoot/src with the template named by current-run requirements. Do not create the test project, add feature code, run dotnet build/test/run, start a browser, or default to a UI template or guessed external-target paths in this step.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Scaffold contract with names, paths, and template constraints.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Solution file and requested .NET application project are present and added to the solution.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Command output, created file list, solution file path, app project path, solution project list, and explicit note that test-project creation and validation are deferred to later setup steps.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Scaffold engineer may adjust command syntax but not the agreed project identity.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block on template failure, unexpected project layout, or generated names that do not match the contract.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a .NET-capable implementer with repository write access.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Solution skeleton change set
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Used by the implementation slice as the baseline solution structure.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include the .slnx or .sln solution file, requested .NET app project under the agreed app directory, selected template/archetype proof, solution membership proof, and confirmation that no test project, feature implementation, dotnet run, browser proof, or app startup was performed in this step.

Steps.Title: Add .NET test project and reference
Steps.Subtitle: Test lane from the start
Steps.Notes: Create the test project using the test framework grounded by the parent contract or existing repository convention, add it to the solution, and reference the application project where appropriate. Do not default to a specific test framework when the current run names another one. Do not implement feature tests, run dotnet build/test/run, start a browser, or perform runtime proof in this step; those belong to validation or feature implementation steps.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Test project is present, added to the solution, and connected to the application project where appropriate.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Project file, solution membership, project reference, package restore or template receipt evidence, and explicit note that runtime/build validation is deferred.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Scaffold engineer can choose command syntax and package defaults for the selected framework but must keep the test project in the same solution.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block if the test project cannot restore or cannot reference the application project when a reference is required.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a .NET-capable implementer with repository write access.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Test project change set
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Used by later implementation slices to add unit tests without reworking structure.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include test project file, solution membership, project reference evidence, and confirmation that no feature tests, dotnet run, browser proof, or app startup was performed in this step.

Steps.Title: Validate first build and test discovery
Steps.Subtitle: Build proof
Steps.Notes: Run restore/build and a targeted test discovery or initial test command so the scaffold is known good before handoff. Do not launch runtime, start a web app, run browser proof, or implement feature behavior in this setup validation step; runtime and browser proof belong to downstream validation steps unless the parent process defines a separate runtime-proof setup step.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Solution skeleton and test project change sets.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Build and test command output that proves the new solution can be iterated safely.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Command, exit code, warnings, and any accepted follow-up risks.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Validation reviewer can reject the scaffold when build proof is missing or non-deterministic.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block on restore/build failure, missing test project, unexplained command output, or artifact recovery when required build or test discovery evidence is missing or invalid before branch routing.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a reviewer capable of interpreting .NET build and test output.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: First build and test discovery evidence
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Used by parent implementation slices to prove the bootstrap baseline is usable.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include command, exit code, relevant output, and unresolved warnings.

Steps.Title: Hand off setup evidence
Steps.Subtitle: Ready for implementation
Steps.Notes: Summarize what was created, what validated, and any residual setup notes the parent process needs.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Validated scaffold outputs and first build evidence.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Handoff packet for the parent development slice.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Created paths, commands run, validation status, and remaining risks.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Setup manager closes only when the validation reviewer evidence is present.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not close with missing build evidence or unresolved scaffold blockers.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind only to a manager-capable operator that can report blockers to the parent run.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Setup handoff packet
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Used by parent runs and future slices to understand the generated solution baseline.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must summarize created paths, commands, validation result, and blockers.
